utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everybody in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Good morning to everyone. May we have begin, as usual, by taking the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Joanna Korner assisted by Jasmina Bosnjakovic, Case Manager, this morning. For the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, Eugene O'Sullivan, and Ms. Tatjana Savic appearing for Stanisic Defence this morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Dragan Krgovic appearing for Zupljanin Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Before we begin today's business, the Chamber has a brief oral decision to deliver.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: On June 24th, the Prosecution filed a motion seeking leave to amend its Rule 65 ter exhibit list by adding the second part of a report authored by upcoming witness Sreto Gajic, ST-204, through whom the Prosecutor intends to tender the report. On June 30th, the Prosecution filed an addendum to the motion. Neither Defence teams has responded to the motion. The Trial Chamber is satisfied that the report, the first part of which is already on the Prosecutor's Rule 65 ter exhibit list, is prima facie relevant and of sufficient importance so as to justify its late addition onto the Prosecution's Rule 65 ter exhibit list. Although disclosed on 23 of June, 2010, the Defence has been aware of the report at least since 22 April 2010 when the Zupljanin Defence first used it in court. The Trial Chamber is therefore satisfied that the addition of the report would not cause undue prejudice to the Defence. Having also considered all other relevant factors for amendments of the Rule 65 ter list, the Trial Chamber is satisfied that granting the request is in the interests of justice and therefore grants the Prosecution leave to add the second part the Gajic report to its Rule 65 ter exhibit list. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's what, actually, I was going to raise. Your Honour, however, both the Defence and I wish to address Your Honours on yesterday's ruling, and we will have to do it today because of the timings given in Your Honours orders. Obviously there is going to be problems, as it appears, over the videolink, so it's better that we start, I think, with the witness. But I would ask that we have 15 minutes before proceedings end today to deal with that matter. I'm asking for 15 because both the Defence and the Prosecution have matters to raise arising out of that decision. The second matter is can I -- can I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Is that about the challenge of adjudicated facts, Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's about your ruling on the witnesses. You delivered, yesterday, a decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Not -- of course, it was not an oral decision because yesterday we were not in court, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. No, it was a written decision, Your Honours. Your Honours, the other matter is I'm sorry to keep pestering you about this, but next week, depending on how long the witnesses actually take, we proposed to call -- we proposed to call Ewa Tabeau. And I now you've been reminded over and over again, but we really do need to know, as do the Defence: Is she an expert, and can we use her report? And, Your Honours, maybe we can leave that to the end as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So whoever -- whichever counsel is on his or her feet at the time at about 1 .30 would remind themselves of the fact that we need take a break.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that we need to take a break in the trial to deal with these matters to which you have alerted us. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I say, I don't any of us have any doubt that this witness will finish within the normal allotted time which is this morning, plus tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: That is useful information. Thank you, Ms. Korner. Because one of the -- we begin with the frustrations caused by the technical problems, so it is -- we -- it's useful learn that that is not going to mean us juggling the time in order to complete this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is, of course, subject to the technical problems being thoroughly solved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The -- lest I forget, before we proceed further, I would wish, for the record, to indicate the Trial Chamber's gratitude for the efforts by Court Management Support Services to overcome the difficulties to which I have alluded and which put us in the position of -- to be to able to begin this witness. And we note also the intrepid trek that our Court Officer had to take to put her in the position where she is now. Her facial response indicate that the works and that she can hear us. Could you confirm that? Thank you. So the -- could you have the witness make the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Microphone not activated] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, sir, you may be seated. I would, first of all, thank you for your coming to assist the Tribunal in its work, and remind you that the solemn declaration that you have just taken means that you could be subject to the penalties which the Tribunal is entitled to impose on persons who give false or incomplete testimony. The -- we also apologise for the further inconvenience which would have, I'm sure, been explained to you as a result of certain technical challenges which we have managed to solve, but now we are ready to begin. And I don't need to ask you whether you can hear me because you have already responded to certain formal questions that have been put. So could you begin by giving us your name, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sreto Gajic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And could you tell us your present occupation, your date of birth, and your ethnicity, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm retired, as of the 1st of March, 2003. I'm a Serb, and I was born on 9th of February, 1952, in Mirkovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Have you testified previously before this Tribunal or before any of the domestic courts in the countries that would have made up the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I have not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, I will explain to you briefly the procedure that will be followed. The side calling you, in this case the Prosecution, would begin by asking you questions. And then counsel for each of the two accused would have a right to cross-examine you. Following that, the Prosecution may have further questions of you, as may the Chamber. Indeed, the Chamber may have questions of you at any time in the course of your examination-in-chief or your cross-examination. The counsel have indicated that it is fully expected that your testimony would be completed by tomorrow. The ordinary sittings of the chamber means that we break for each day at 1.45 local time. But between when we begin and when we break, there are breaks to accommodate the technical requirements of taping the proceedings and things of that nature. If, however, for any reason, you need a break to -- before the ordinary time that we would rise to accommodate those things, you would indicate that to the Court Officer who will -- who will then let us know and we will certainly accommodate you. And with that, I will invite counsel for the Prosecution to begin her examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, before I do that can I ask: Are we sticking to the normal break time, in other words, about 10.25?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I always think that -- I always bear in mind, apart from counsel's convenience, the accused, whose routine would have been premised on the usual breaks, so that is what I do plan to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic, I want to begin by dealing very shortly with your background. Did you, from 1984 until the beginning of April of 1992, work for the -- the SUP, as it then was, of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And were you, in fact, a police inspector in Sarajevo SUP working on defence preparations?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Defence preparations of the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, sorry, I should have said that. And just so that we understand it, was -- was its function to organise, to manage, and to train police personnel for the purposes of national Defence?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Well, that was the work that involved organisation, training, professional training, and materiel for the entire police force which was the militia, called the militia then, for the active duty and the reserve force.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did that involve any type of partition -- partition, sorry. Did that involve any type of coordination and participation in joint exercises with the military?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: They were joint exercises at the level of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, as that was then, and units of the Territorial Defence took part. Or, rather, the police had its own exercises. We were independent and autonomous compared to the other participants.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. During those exercises that were carried out, was there any element of resubordination by the police to military command?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: That was governed by the Law on National Defence. It regulated matters of that kind. However, those situations were very rare, and I don't ever remember actually it happening. There was no resubordination, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. That's all I want to ask you about that. Now, after the division of the MUP, did you, in fact, around the 10th of April, go with your family to Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did you stay there until the beginning of May of 1992, when you went to the headquarters of the Serbian MUP, Serbian Republic MUP, which were, at that stage, in Vrace?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did you there see Cedo Kljajic who was, at the time, the head of the public security, as it were, the head of public security at headquarters level?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Cedo Kljajic was the under-secretary, or, rather, the head of the public security section, so I reported to him and he appointed me head of the defence preparations of police section, as chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So that was effectively the same job you'd been doing in the old BiH MUP. Did you just do defence preparations again, or did you undertake other tasks?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: It was more or less the same kind of work that I'd done previously, although I was a sort of leader, being the chief. I was an inspector in the secretariat, beforehand, but at the time, I didn't actually work on defence preparations. I quite simply carried out the assignments I was given by my superior. And I've already told that to the investigators. I had to write certain dispatches and other documents, information, reports, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And who would instruct you to write these dispatches?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: The chief of the police administration was Milos Zuban. So he was my superior, and he assigned me tasks. He told me when to write dispatches or analyse documents and things like that. So most of my assignments came from Zuban, and I was in the police administration, and the head of that administration was Milan [as interpreted] Zuban.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think that it -- that's Milos Zuban, is that right, Z-u-b-a-n?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Milos Zuban.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, these dispatches that you were writing, to whom were they being sent?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: They were usually sent to the public security centres or stations.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And did you get responses from the public security centres?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Well, since that was a period of time where there were quite lot of problems in setting up communications, sometimes they would arrive on time, sometimes they would arrive late, and, at times, they never arrived and then we had to use telephone communication. But, in principle, those dispatches did reach their destination, and we received feedback, a response. But as I say, there were a lot of problems during that period of time with the establishing communications and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. The sort of information that you -- that was being requested in these dispatches, what sort of areas did it cover?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Well, it's difficult for me to remember now because it was a long time ago, but mostly they were related to a situation report, involving who to send -- looking at the law and order situation and what the problems were in that regard. Various violations were committed, whether by police members or anybody else, whether police had to be called in. Then you had the battle-front. We would send out information about the number of persons injured. Well, the topics were very varied. I can't remember all of them because it's been a long time since then. But that's what we sent dispatches for. Dispatches are very short, brief; you couldn't write a long dispatch, especially not at the time. So just in a few sentences, we would size up the situation and report on it. So we would summarise and send out brief pieces of information.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When you received responses, to whom did you pass on those responses?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: The responses that came in, as I say, I was one of the people working in the police administration. But, any way, the head had to be informed with the response. Now where this was forwarded to, did it go to the analytics department to be studied and analysed and then reports written and sent on to the minister, I'm not quite sure. But we would gather the information together, collect up all the dispatches, analyse them, process them, and then it was decided whether it would go to the minister's office or some other administration. So that's roughly what happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The minister, Mico Stanisic, was he at Vrace while you were there?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: He appeared very rarely.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When you say "very rarely," you were at Vrace for what, for a period of -- well, until moved from -- to Lukavica; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't quite remember. But, yes. Yes, that's it. I can't give you a date, whether it was two months. So don't hold me to that. I don't remember exactly. But it was roughly May and maybe the first part of June. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. During -- you say he was there rarely. Can you give us a rough estimate? I appreciate it's a long time. Was he there once a week, twice a week? Less or more?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't really say. If we're talking about averages, perhaps once in ten days. Or perhaps I didn't notice him and he might have been there. But as far as I remember, for about ten days. As far as I could know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And as you say, logically he might have been there and you didn't see him. Now, I want to move on, please, to the reports that you did, the inspection reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And can we start, please, with looking at a document which, in your binder, is, I believe, tab 2; and the 65 ter number is -- it is actually already an exhibit, 1D00176.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now this is an order with a very --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If we go to the last -- second page B/C/S, second page in English. Yeah. Very, very bad copy I'm afraid, and it's not possible, really, to see the signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But had you seen -- had you actually seen Mico Stanisic's signature?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, yes, I did see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So are you able to say whether that's his signature or not? If you're not - and I agree it's a very bad copy - then say so straight away.

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: It's a poor copy. The signature not very legible, and I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's fair enough. Now, this order relates - if we go to the first page, please, in both English and in B/C/S - dated the 27th of July, and the number of this order is 10-17/92. In paragraph 2, he is ordering that immediately the removal of individuals who have been held criminally responsible for crimes that are officially prosecuted (except for political and verbal offences). As a matter of interest, Mr. Gajic, are you able to tell what you say was meant by "political offences"?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I assume, but I'm not sure, that it's probably in the sense of political orientation or some kind of political or national or ethnic orientation. I assume this, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Probably it was a politically delicate [as interpreted] matter from the previous system.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, I was going ask you that. But it's refer -- because in the previous system you couldn't belong to a nationalist party?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm really sorry. Before the witness answers, I don't think that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You don't think it was recorded?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I don't think that -- that what he says was probably properly recorded in his previous answer, page 12, 12/13 lines, he said I think he was -- he was mentioning a political delict.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Delict?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Which is, I agree, different.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Gajic, did you -- could you just tell us, when I asked you what was meant by "political," you -- you answered that it was probably in the sense of political orientation or some kind of political or national or ethnic orientation. And then you went on to say: "Probably," and this is how it's been recorded, "it was a politically delicate matter." Did you use the word "delicate," or some other word?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Not delicate. Delicate is something different. It has a different meaning. What I said was "political delict." I assume that what was meant was the orientation from a previous system. All the police staff who worked in that system were forbidden from being a member of any political party. And since most of them were members of the League of Communists, they didn't have to be, so, simply, they could not be held responsible on that basis. We were all accepted and could work normally in this Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. It then goes on to say that the surplus of available individuals referred to in items 1, which was the optimum number, and those who were referred to in paragraph 2 should be placed at the disposal of the army. And then 4: "Immediately disband and place under the command of the army of the Serbian republic all special units formed during the war in areas of Security Services Centre [sic]." And it goes on to say what should happen to the people in there. Now, were aware at headquarters that a number of special police units also been formed at the level of the Security Services Centres and sometimes below?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I'm not really able to answer this question, since I wasn't in that inner leadership of the ministry. I -- some information did reach me through the chief or something like that. But I knew more or less that some centres had special units but not that stations had that as well. I didn't have that information at my disposal, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear about something called intervention squads or intervention platoons that were maintained at the level of some of the SJBs?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't hear that at the time. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's go on, please, to the next paragraph because this is the one that I want to ask you about in particular. Paragraph 6, which is on the second page in English and B/C/S: "The execution of this order and the provision of specialist assistance in the Autonomous Region of Krajina shall be overseen by the chief of police affairs, Milos Zuban; in the SAO Semberija by ... Cedo Kljajic; ... Herzegovina by Draskovic ... and Mr. Vukovic ... in the SAO of Northern Bosnia by Mr. --" I think that should be Kusmuk - is that right? - and then, "in Romanija-Birac ... Mr. Radovic." Now as we're going to see, in fact it was you who went to the Autonomous Region of Krajina, and not Mr. Zuban. How did that come about?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I was just assigned to go to Banja Luka. I don't know the reasons for that. When we're talking about the Ministry of the Interior, there is a hierarchy there, and orders have to be respected and carried out.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Before you went, as we will see, to Banja Luka --

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I think that Milos Zuban went to Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, I should -- actually, I should have asked you this first of all: Who assigned you to go to Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Before we went to Banja Luka, there was meeting, as far as I can remember, a meeting was scheduled. I assume that Milos Zuban informed about it. I don't know who else it could have been. Informed me to attend this meeting, where we received brief instructions about what we were supposed to do in the field.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm going to come to the meeting and who was there. But had you been told before the meeting that you were to go to Banja Luka to implement this order, or to oversee the implementation of the order?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I really cannot remember. I cannot answer that question. I don't know if I was informed before the meeting or on the actual day of the meeting. I really cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's move to the meeting. But this stage, end of July and early August, had the headquarters of the Serbian MUP moved to Jahorina?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, we were in Jahorina then.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And do you remember where exactly the meeting took place?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but I think it was at Kosuta. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And who was at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure if I will manage to list all the people. I don't think so. But I think it was Mr. Zuban who was there. I was there. I think Njegus was there, Radovan Njegus. I'm not sure if Cedo Kljajic was there or not. I don't remember. I don't know. I simply cannot remember. It's been a long time since then, and I really cannot say something that I'm not sure about.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. You said Mr. Njegus, Radovan. Was that Radomir Njegus who was head of the administration?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Radomir, Radomir.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Radomir Njegus.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what --

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I think that he was the chef de cabinet at the time. I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The chef de cabinet to ... to whom?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I think he was the chef de cabinet to the minister when we were at Vrace. When we moved to Jahorina, I don't remember whether he was chief of the personnel administration. I don't remember. But I think by that time he was the chief of the personnel administration. But this is something that can be checked.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What about the minister? Was the minister there at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I can't remember, no. I can't remember whether the minister was there or not. All I know is that the minister was there when we came back, when we drafted the report. Then I remember the minister being there. I cannot remember whether he was there at this first meeting or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, do you remember making a statement to the investigator about this meeting?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: The meeting was discussed. The investigator asked me about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Would it help you to refresh your memory about who was actually present at the meeting and, indeed, who spoke, if you had a chance to look at your statement?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did look at the statement. I think there is a statement here, too, so I'm going to ask --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... if you -- yes, if you look --

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: -- if can I look at my statement, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, you can. Could you look, please, at tab -- it's at tab 1. And you will find, on the second page -- or, sorry, it's page 3 at the bottom, paragraph 17.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We can put it up for the purposes of the Defence. It's, in e-court, as 9033. And it's the third page in both the English and the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I comment?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Of course. First of all, just before you comment, do you see paragraph 17 of the statement that you made?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And do you say there that the meeting in Jahorina was attended by Minister Stanisic, as well as the other people you've mentioned, Cedo Kljajic, not sure; Radomir Njegus; Milos Zuban; and somebody called Rade Radovic?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I said earlier in the statement that I wasn't sure. But it's possible that he was there. The statement that I gave to the Prosecutor, I signed that statement in the English version, not the Serbian version. And I was quite categorical when I said that, while giving the statement, but it's possible that he was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, again --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's been a long time since then, so it's really not possible to remember everything.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just pause for a moment, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Page 17, line 22. I believe the witness says, I don't know how categorical I was when I said that. Maybe this can be clarified with the witness. I heard him say that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, I think -- as I said before, I think it would be better if you simply ask us to repeat it, rather than saying what you heard, but.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, did you say you were quite categorical when you said that, or did you say something else? In other words, when you said, in giving the statement - which, I agree, you -- was read back to you and you signed in English - did you -- were you -- did you say to the Court you were being categorical, or did you say something different?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: The statement that I gave to the Prosecutor, I signed the English version of the statement, not the Serbian version. And the interpreter read back the statement to me in the Serbian. When I gave the statement, regarding the presence of Stanisic, I said that I wasn't sure. I said that I don't know how categorical I was in the sense of mentioning Minister Stanisic. I don't know how categorical I was, how convincing I was, or convinced in what I was saying. I don't know how categorical I was. Please believe me, I cannot remember all of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I'll come back to the meeting. But, Mr. Gajic, were you not seen about a week ago, on the 8th of July, by the same investigator who took your statement, and a lawyer was present as well, and did you -- were you then given the opportunity to read the statement because it was -- it had been translated?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I was given the opportunity, and I read the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... exactly. And you --

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I don't know if that was my mistake, or perhaps I didn't pay enough attention. I mean, I really cannot answer now. I don't know what to say now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yeah, because you did make a number of corrections. You obviously read it carefully because you corrected how you described --

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether it's a lack of experience in testifying or something. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just wait a moment. You see, you did correct a number of matters.

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did make a few corrections.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But you didn't correct this one. Do you agree? You didn't say, I know - just wait for a moment so I can finish my question - you didn't say, I know I said in the statement that Mico Stanisic was there, but now I can't say that I'm sure, did you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, I would remind you that the -- this -- we're in the area of the witness refreshing his memory.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Only. And the -- although you sometime back -- we have on the record a question which, in my view, shouldn't have been -- did you say the -- so the actual paragraph 17 was put to him. I think that that's as far as it can go. The evidence is what the witness is testifying to now, and he has explained why there are any discrepancies, as there do appear to be discrepancies. And I don't know that this matter can be taken any further.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, he's saying -- what I think he was agreeing that what he said was that he couldn't be categorical about it. And I'm merely asking him why, in that event, if he didn't, when he re-read the statement, he couldn't be categorical. A week ago, he didn't correct it. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We have an answer, so let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't know that we do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I think the witness said twice that he simply couldn't remember whether Mr. Stanisic was or was not present at the meeting, and that's as far as we can take it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You're saying, now, while testifying, you -- you can't be sure whether or not Mr. Stanisic was present? Is that right, sir? Think back to that meeting.

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Earlier I explained. I don't know how many times I explained. Simply, I cannot guarantee 100 per cent and assert that he was present. Yes, it's true that that is said in the statement and that I didn't intervene about this seven days ago. It was perhaps an oversight on my part, but I cannot claim with 100 per cent -- with 100 per cent certainty that he was present at the first meeting. He was present at the second meeting, however.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, then, can I just ask you please, now, to look at paragraph 19 of your statement, which is on the next page where you say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: No, Ms. Korner, not time. The -- this is not an exhibit. The way the question should be asked is you refer him to the paragraph and then ask the question. But don't read -- this is not an exhibit. It is not likely to become an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Read the paragraph to yourself, please, Mr. Gajic. Do you see what you say there?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I've read it, and I can see what is stated there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I said earlier that I wasn't 100 per cent sure that he was there, but I do remember that at the meeting there was word about the unit having to be disbanded, but there was no mention of the reasons for that, specifically. Only the reasons why that unit had to be disbanded specifically at the Banja Luka centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Well, first of all --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: If -- we're at the point where we should take the break, Ms. Korner. You seem to be moving on to something -- not something new but a different part of the same question, so this would probably be a convenient point. We would resume in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Korner, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, just dealing, Mr. Gajic, with what you told the investigators at paragraph 19. And you said that somebody - this was your last answer - there was word about the unit having to be disbanded, but there was no mention of the reasons for this special, only the reasons why the unit had to be disbanded specifically at the Banja Luka centre. Now, what was the reason that was given to you as to why the Banja Luka Centre Special Police Unit had to be disbanded?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, not only at Banja Luka Centre, but all the centres. So it was a general instruction for all special units, which, at that time, existed in the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And it applied to units first and foremost, as far as I can remember -- well, local politics had influenced their formation in the first place, and certain crimes were being committed or had been committed in town. Nothing specific. But in the field, just to take a look at everything that was found, but that they had to be disbanded. So nothing specific, but just some -- well, there was no mention of those acts and what the units did at the meeting, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, just pause for a moment, please, sir --

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Because, at that time, there was a lot of theft, looting, and things of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Please tell me, Who was -- certain crimes had been committed, were being committed, or had been committed by whom?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Well, if some of the members, especially the special units that were established then, if some of their member - if you understand me -- well, they were to be disbanded, quite simply. And then those members prosecuted. And you'll see, further on, who was supposed to take the unit over. Now, I don't know the details or the specifics of it all, so it concerned some of the members or members of the police that engaged in crime, so they had to be placed at the army's disposal, they had to be prosecuted, let go, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. You said, earlier on: "Certain crimes were being committed or had been committed in town." In which town?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Because the emphasis was on that. And this something that at the meeting I ... I'm experiencing interruption in the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Did -- did --

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I couldn't hear the interpretation properly. There was interference.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. The question I asked you was: Earlier you said that crimes were being committed, and you've clarified, "by the special police in town." In which town?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I didn't say "in town." I said quite simply where the special police was active. I don't know where it was active. I don't know where it was engaged, on what territory, in which parts. I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you told at this meeting --

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I wasn't interested in where the special unit was, for instance, where it was deployed. There was a report on its work, in the work of the special police, and that report was placed ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, were you told at that first meeting who had made the decision to disband the special police unit? Or units, in the plural.

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I don't know if I understood it correctly or formulated it correctly, but I said that it was the Presidency of Republika Srpska or the Serbian Republic. Whether it was at an Assembly meeting, or where the decision was taken, that's what I said. But it was the leadership of Republika Srpska which took the decision to disband them. That's the important thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And who at this meeting gave you, firstly, the information that the president of the Republika Srpska had made the decision to disband the units and the reasons for the disbanding; namely, that they were committing crimes? Who told you that?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: In my statement I said that Mr. Stanisic said that. Now whether it was Mr. Kljajic, any way, one of the two. Now, from paragraph 17, I recount the acts linked to point 19. And it says Stanisic told us, we were told by Stanisic, who made the decision and issued tasks. If it wasn't him, then it's Kljajic. One of the two. And as I'm not certain now, I'm not 100 per cent certain that it was Mr. Stanisic now. But one of the two must have.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. So there's the meeting --

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Because I was the person executing, implementing the decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And did you then go, after this meeting, to Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Now whether it was the next day, I'm not quite sure. I don't remember the date. But, anyway, with Mr. Josic; I think he went with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we look, please, now at your first report, which you will find behind tab 8, and it's P631. And if we go to the last page in each document, which is page 5 in English and also in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do we see that you -- you submitted this report on the 5th of August, and it was done by you and Mr. Mirosavic. Was he one of your inspectors.

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Let's go to the first page again. We see that this is pursuant to the order, which is the one we looked at a few minutes ago of the 27th of July, 1992. You carry out the inspection of CSB Banja Luka and the SJB in Prijedor and Banja Luka. Did you, in fact, visit the premises of both the CSB - and the SJB Banja Luka was in the same building, we've been told - and Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I went to see the chief of the public security station of Banja Luka, Mr. Turkusa [phoen], and I went to the Prijedor Public Security Station, the late Simo Drljaca.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yeah, well -- sorry, you said Mr. Turkusa; was it Mr. Tutus who was the chief of the public security station?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Not the centre. He was chief of the public security station of Banja Luka, and Mr. Stojan Zupljanin was the chief of the centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. All right. Yes, thank you. All right. We see at the second paragraph of your report, between the 2nd and 4th of August, the two of you had a meeting, apparently -- or had meetings with the chief, that's Stojan Zupljanin of the CSB Banja Luka and then his close associates. Now, first of all, can we look at the bottom of the first page where you say that: "... SJB Prijedor has set aside 300 police employees for securing the camps, Keraterm, Omarska, Trnopolje, where war prisoners are held." Who gave you that information?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: The late Simo Drljaca.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And he gave you the actual names of the camps, or were you already aware of the names of these camps?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I think -- I didn't know. He told me. But I think the meeting - but I'm not quite sure, so don't hold me to that - I think that Marko Djenadija was at the meeting too, who was one of his associates, and that they provided that information.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Before you were given this information, were you aware that the Prijedor police were running camps for war prisoners?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you consider that an important piece of information, that the Prijedor police were actually running camps?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will object to that because in this report, which was quoted to the witness, was said the police secure the camp, not running the camp. The -- so that's the -- why the witness is confused.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much, Mr. Krgovic. And no doubt the witness has heard you and you can explain exactly what's going through his mind, but I'd be grateful if we didn't have interruptions like that, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Except, Ms. Korner, that the observation Mr. Krgovic has made means that perhaps you should --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm going to rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: My objection is to the witness effectively being given an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I understand that. I take your point.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You say in your report SJB Prijedor has set aside 300 police employees for securing the camps. And if we go over to the next page in English, though it's still the same page in your language, you say: "Based on the statement by the chief of the station, arrangements were being made with officials from the 1st Krajina Corps and the Crisis Staff of Prijedor municipality regarding the takeover of the camps security by the Army of the Serbian Republic. However, a solution to this issue has not yet been found." Now, what did you understand and what did you mean by writing in your report that 300 police employees were securing these three camps?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Well, in view of the fact that, in principle, I know why -- what the police was intended for, this is an absurdity that happened, that such a large number of employees were to be set aside from the service in order to secure the camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... yes, but --

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Because the police is mostly there to keep law and order, to protect property, and all the other tasks it has, not having to enumerate them. So these people were freed of those responsibilities, freed of that load.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. As you've just pointed out -- we'll go back to my original question. You just pointed out that the police were there to keep law and order, to protect property, et cetera. Did you consider that the information you were being given, that instead of dealing with law and order, the police were - and I'll use your word - "securing the camps," to be an important piece of information?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Well, certainly the information that I got from the chief of the public security station I thought to be important, and that's why I included it in my report. And for the police to justify its role and carry out its duties, it needed to be freed of the obligations that were to be taken on by someone else.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. When you were being told this, you said in the second paragraph we looked at that present at the meetings were the chief of the CSB Banja Luka and his close associates, in other words, the chiefs of the SJBs, was Stojan Zupljanin there when you were being given this information by Drljaca or his sidekick?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: No. Drljaca gave me the information in Prijedor, not in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. The paragraph that I've just read to you about arrangements being made with officials from the 1st Krajina Corps and the Crisis Staff of Prijedor municipality, who told you that arrangements were being made about the takeover of the camps' security by the army?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Drljaca.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Did you -- later we'll see you were at meetings which were attended by the army. Did you have any discussions with the army about whether this was true or not, or whether any arrangements had been made?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: No talks with the army linked to taking over the security of these camps. I didn't attend any talks, nor were they conducted in my presence. Now, who attended those meetings, I really don't know. But in my presence -- or, rather, I did not attend meetings of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Well, let's go on to the -- apparently the purpose of your visit, and that is the special police. In the third paragraph, they -- there was a discussion about the order from Mico Stanisic that those who committed crimes should be removed and put at the disposal of the army. And then: "With regards to realisation mentioned under point 2" -- sorry, it's the next page in B/C/S for you. It's the same page in English for us. If you turn to the next page. It's the second paragraph, and it says: "With regards to realisation mentioned under point 2 of the order issued by the ministry, the chief of the CSB Banja Luka Stojan Zupljanin requests further explanation of the word "removed," in case it refers to the termination of employment which is the way I understood it. I would like this to be confirmed in a dispatch." Now, is what you're saying there that Stojan Zupljanin said to you, I don't understand what you mean by "removed," or what the minister's order means?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Would you tell me which paragraph it is in Serbian, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The part I'm reading from ... sorry. In Serbian, I have just read the part of the paragraph that is at the -- towards the end of the paragraph that's the first one on the second page.

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, the one you've just read out. Where can I find that?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You can find that in page 2 in the document. 0360-5786 is stamped at the top, and the very last bit of that paragraph is what I have just read out to you.

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And my question, I'll repeat it: Is the minister's original order, which we looked at with you, says: "I hereby order immediately to remove ..." What I'm asking you is: Are you saying in this paragraph of the report that Stojan Zupljanin said to you, I do not understand what is meant by the word remove?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Well, from the report -- first of all, I apologise, but the interpretation is coming in with interruptions. There's interference. So please understand me if I don't understand -- always understand your question and I ask you to repeat, because there's interference. And now I'll explain what you just asked me. From the report, and in the report it says that Stojan, up to a point, was not clear on what the word "removed" meant. That's how I understand -- I understand it as termination of employment, which meant that there would be termination of employment but placed at the disposal of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm -- I'm terribly sorry, Ms. Korner, but line -- page 9 [sic], line 4, I don't think that the -- the witness said "I understand it." Maybe you can clarify that with him. I think he used -- I'm sure he used the other word.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you say, sir, a moment ago, as you said in your report, that you understood the word "removed" to mean termination of employment?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I think I said that from this it follows that Stojan didn't understand properly and asked what the word removed meant, and I, then, explained to him and said that, in actual fact, it meant termination of employment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, that's what my question was. He said to you, I don't understand what the word "removed" means. That's what he actually said to you?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether he said it that way. I can't remember his -- Stojan's exact words, Madam Prosecutor. But from this report it follows that it wasn't clear what the word "odstraniti," "removed," meant. So I said that it was termination of employment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Can you, in this context, Mr. Gajic --

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: As it says in the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can you, Mr. Gajic, in this context, as an experienced police officer, and given the order, think of anything else that "removed" could have meant?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't really know what else it could mean. It's not an object, you understand, of some material nature, and then say, Throw it away or remove it. It's a living being, and you know what is done with such a person.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. All right. Let's go on with this report. You then, in the next paragraph, give an explanation about since the beginning of the war, the -- self-styled units and various groups had been operating. The Krajina government reached a decision on forming the special police detachment within CSB Banja Luka, consisting of 162 members, and so on and so forth. Was that information you already had, or was that given to you by Mr. Zupljanin or his associates?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I received that information at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And it goes on to say this: "The centre chief and his associates, as well as the inner command of this unit, have, at a meeting held on 2nd and 4th of August ... emphasised all positive results as well as negativities the unit faced starting with its involvement in combat currently in the area of the Kotor Vares municipality and leading to suspension of a number of employees and initiation of criminal proceedings ..." What were the positive results he was emphasising?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: This mostly referred to their combat engagement, since I know that members of the police or the militia at the time participated in combat actions, so mainly and exclusively on their combat engagement, maintaining the lines, movement of the enemy, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what were the negative ones?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: In any case, I think that you probably have at your disposal information about activities of the special unit. The negativities due to which disciplinary proceedings were initiated had to do with what I said was mentioned at this meeting: thefts, robberies. It was mostly in relation to these kind of acts. It was nothing specific. I didn't ask individually by name against whom a criminal report was submitted, the reasons for submitting such a criminal report. I didn't go into that. And it wasn't my assignment or my job either to go into individual case details.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm terribly sorry again. 11, 7, I think the witness said something different. Concerning the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, you said a moment ago that I think you probably have at your disposal information about the activities of the special unit the negativities due to which disciplinary proceedings were initiated. Did you say that, or did you say something different?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I said that you probably have as an attachment, and I don't, but I remember the information about the work of the special unit, because, as an attachment to this report, I provided a report on the work of the CSB Banja Luka and information about the activities of the CSB Banja Luka Special Unit for you to be able to have that information, at least I assume so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I'm, at the moment, just concerned with what he actually said to you about the negative ones, and you say it was to do with looting, thefts, and robberies. Did he ever mention the fact that his special police had been involved in killings outside combat?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Looting, robberies, yes, yes. In that sense.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I'm asking you: Did he ever mention that his police, allegedly, were involved in killings?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: No. No, that was never told to me, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And then he -- he wanted the CSB Banja Luka to have a special police unit --

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Once again, I state with full responsibility before this Trial Chamber that this was never told to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm -- I'm not disputing that, sir. Anyhow, he then made proposals or conclusions, as chief of the CSB, which we can see you set out as 1, 2, and 3. And then if you go, please -- you need to go to the next page in B/C/S; page 3, also for us, in English, and B/C/S. You say, During the stay at SJB Banja Luka, the conclusion reached by station officials regarding the issue of the special police unit is that the same needs to be immediately disbanded. And one of the reasons, according to them, is that until the beginning of the war, in the area of Banja Luka, there was seven crimes committed. And since the formation of the SOS, the name of this unit, 65 crimes were committed. Now, the first question is: Is this what you were being told by the SJB officials in the absence of the CSB officials?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Just give me a moment, please. This is something that was said at the chiefs of the public security station [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. What -- what I'm trying to understand, what the Court may need to understand is: Are you saying that the SJB Banja Luka was -- contrary to - just listen, please. Don't answer - was saying, contrary to what Mr. Zupljanin wanted, namely, that they should be kept on, or a special unit should be kept on, they should be disbanded?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I am receiving a very bad sound of the interpretation. It's constantly interrupted. Can you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In this paragraph which I hope you've now read and which I read out to you, was the SJB saying to you, you should disband these -- or this unit should be disbanded because it's responsible for the increase in crimes, which was contrary to what Mr. Zupljanin wanted?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I understood the question very well now because the connection was good. In any event, the chief of the public security station in Banja Luka was categorical that the unit should be disbanded.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: As to whether he had all the indicators, including the positive ones of the unit, I don't know. As opposed to Stojan Zupljanin who agreed that it should be disbanded, but he wasn't as categorical immediately in his initial statements. However, he did agree that this unit should be disbanded.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Then -- but, can I ask you next: The SOS, the name of the unit, who told you that the unit supposedly of special police was actually called the SOS?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember now who mentioned the name, but it was stated at the meeting then what the name of the unit was that was formed by a decision of the Krajina government.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry, I want to make this clear. Is what -- is the information that you got, because this begins about the special police unit, that this special police unit was also known as the SOS?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I was informed at the meeting that the name of it was SOS.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Now, very quickly, because I want to deal with the other report that you wrote, you then say that -- in the next paragraph, that there was a complaint there was insufficient communication from -- from the ministry, no requests, and no clear views on certain issues. For example -- or brackets, what to do with employees of Muslim nationality. SJB Banja Luka has made the decision on annual leave to be used by these employees. Just very briefly, please, explain what you mean by that sentence.

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Where is that?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You will find that in the -- below the paragraph we've just been looking at on page 3.

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me which paragraph that is that you're reading, which paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Page 3, third paragraph.

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Last sentence.

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Should I comment?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. What do you mean by: "SJB Banja Luka has made the decision on annual leave to be used by those employees."? Namely, those of Muslim -- Muslim nationality.

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Simply, the employee would be given a decision to use his holidays for the period as provided under the law.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you mean he was told to take his annual leave? How long was the period?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I didn't have the decisions of -- for those workers who were told that, but I was informed about it at the meeting, that those workers had been given decisions to use their annual leave. According to their qualifications or years of service, each employee was given a certain number of annual leave days to use. I think that is how I was informed. It was not for some indefinite period of time. From what I could understood [as interpreted], these were annual leave days that are provided for under the law. That's how I understood it at least.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, quite. Why was this something which was being raised with you, and what -- why should the -- the question, What is to be done with employees of Muslim nationality, be raised?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I think that you could see from the entire order that an overall situation was being viewed from the organisation of the centre, the status, replenishment, staffing, criminal acts, and so on. So probably our reasons were also to inform me, among other things, about that matter as well, which is something that I noted in my report and delivered to the minister's office, including the things that I had undertaken in regard to that matter. My task was to review these things and to submit a report and not to indicate or do anything that I was not specifically authorised to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I'll try one last time. Why was there any problem that you were told about that with police officers working at the SJB Banja Luka who were Muslims? What was the problem?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I really don't know. Please believe me, I'm not acquainted with that. I mean, perhaps I can state a private opinion, a private opinion. I don't know if you're interested in that. But as for what the problem was there, that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. We haven't got time to continue on this. Then you go on in the next paragraph: "CSB Banja Luka has compiled a six-month report on its work, and the same is enclosed with the information." We'll look at that very quickly in a second. And then you make your recommendations: "I propose the following:" And we can see those recommendation [sic], that the remainder of the 24 SJBs should be inspected. Number 3 - if we go to the next page in English, please, and if you turn over in the Serbian language. 3 is proposing a CSB to be established in Prijedor. Then, 5 is to do with the CSB Banja Luka. 6, you put forward Mr. Zupljanin's proposal that there's a special unit and initiate adequate proceeding against those members who have ruined the reputation of the unit. And then 7: "Urgently make contact with the Army of the SR BiH command and consider the issue of jurisdiction over camps security on the territory of Prijedor municipality." Now, you said this was -- report was for the office of the minister. To whom did you actually deliver this report?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I don't remember, but I think that the report was sent to the cabinet, the office of the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, can we look very quickly, please, at the document which you should have had inserted behind that. It's 8A, and it's Exhibit P595.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It was sent down to Sarajevo by e-mail, and we got confirmation that it had been given to the Court Officer. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is that the -- all I want you to do is confirm, sir, that that's the report that you sent up with your report.

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Let me just look at my report to see if it is the correct title. Yes, it's my report that is being cited. Let me just check whether that title is correct. It's my report that I submitted to the minister, the one that we were looking at earlier on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter's note that there is a lot of background noise making it a bit difficult to hear.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Did you attach, sir -- I know it's your report; we've all agreed that. What I'm asking you is whether, when you say you were sending your report on the work of the CSB Banja Luka, is it the report you've now -- looking at -- no, no -- in your hand?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Just one moment. Just one moment, please. Yes, that is the report. I assume -- yes, that is the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. Right. Now, can you look now, please --

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I didn't read it. I just attached that to my report and left it at the office. I didn't read this report.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, sir. I'm not concerned about that. But I want you to look, please, next at a document which is your tab 6.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And it is P1010.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, this is a document, is it, that -- dated the 3rd of August, and addressed to the minister. And you say: "Pursuant to the discussions that you held on the 3rd of August, 1992, with Stojan Zupljanin, chief of the Banja Luka CSB, and regarding the implementation of your order ... we hereby suggest that Tomo Mirosavic and I continue working in the [sic] centre until the 5th of August ..." What discussions did Mico Stanisic have with Stojan Zupljanin? Are we talking about a personal discussion, or something that you've been told about?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Since I couldn't do all of the tasks planned for that one day in the order of the minister, and I spoke with Mr. Zupljanin about that, and then he got in touch with the minister, and I had to ask by dispatch for permission to continue for a day or two more to be able to complete the tasks given to me by the minister. So, in that -- that is what this dispatch is about.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Were you present when Zupljanin spoke to Mico Stanisic, or did he just tell you that he had spoken to him?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I wasn't present. I was told -- I mean, he probably told me that he spoke with him, but I didn't actually -- I wasn't present during that conversation, because I couldn't say something else in the dispatch, had somebody else conducted that conversation. In the dispatch it says that Stojan Zupljanin spoke with the minister. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, all right. Yes. Thank you, sir. That's all I ask about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, in fact, for some reason it was MFI'd, so can I ask that it now be fully exhibited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The exhibit is de-MFI'd, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm not sure there's such a word, but we get the general idea.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we now look, please, at the second part of your report, which you will find at -- behind tab number 11. Sorry. Do I mean number 11? Just a moment. No, I mean number 9. I'm so sorry. 9. Oh, and, sorry, it's 10394, 65 ter.

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: That's not it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Behind tab 9. It should be dated Sarajevo, the 10th of August. And it's actually, I think, signed by you, if you look at the last page.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we look at the last page in English, and -- it's page 4 in English; page 3 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You then -- if we go back to the first page, you talk about meetings that were held at Banja Luka and Prijedor on the 7th and 9th of August. And the first meeting on the 7th and 8th, Stojan Zupljanin was there; Djuro Bulic, chief of the SJB, the public security sector in the centre; and Mr. Samardzija, the special police detachment assistant commander; then Mr. Samara, a inspector. And on 9th of August, the following joined: Colonel Bogojevic, chief of the 1st Krajina Corps, military security, and command of the special police detachment. Now, after introducing a decision made by the minister of the interior at a meeting held on the 6th of August, a large number of participants, and in particular members of the special police detachment command and platoon commanders, rejected all suggestions and in -- and insisted on preserving the status of the unit as it was. Who do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Exclusively the command, not the commander. The command of the special unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yeah. But you say here: "... a large" --

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: And I think that the commander was very pig-headed, as we like to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, you mention Mr. Samardzija as being present. Who else was present from the special police?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I think his name was Lukic. He was an officer, if I remember correctly. But don't hold me to that. I think his name was Lukic and he was a captain by rank. Now, who else was there, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. So you then go on to say: "Following a lengthy discussion and presentation of a number of facts which contributed to the disbanding of special and other units" --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, that's the second page in English and still on the first page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: "The following conclusion was reached by Banja Luka CSB chief and Colonel Bogojevic who had previously appraised General Talic, 1st Krajina Corps commander of the entire situation, and apparently it is agreed that the special police detachment will be put at the disposal of the 1st Krajina Corps." And there was -- then it goes on to say, after item 5 -- you need to go to the second page for you, Mr. Gajic. "Based on their continuous visits to police and crime prevention operatives, the chief of the Security Services Centre and his associates stated that in public security stations in the area of the centre's activities there are no special or other units." What did you understand him to mean by "no special or other units"? By the word "other"?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Well, that there are no units of that type or any other units which acted on the territory of the public security stations. So none of the stations, none of the public security stations, according to what they said, disposed of those types of unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: A type of special police unit, even if under another name?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, then, if we carry on, there's then -- your report deals with the activities or the complaints about the activities of the light brigades. And then you go on to deal with the question of the camps.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we go to the third page in English. And it's still the second page in your report.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, this meeting, apparently, with the Krajina Corps representative and the rest, was on the 7th and 8th of August. By that stage, were you aware that television newsreel film had been made showing Omarska and Trnopolje? Television film by foreign journalists.

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: And what's the question?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When you held this meeting, were you and the other participants aware of the fact that there had been newsreel footage on television from international journalists - British ones, in particular - of the camp at Omarska and the camp at Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I didn't know. Now whether others knew, I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. There's then a description of what Omarska is, and it states: "About 175 persons are in the centre which are being secured by about 40 police officers from Prijedor SJB. Following the completion of the investigation process ... the persons will be transferred to Manjaca." Now, was this being said at the meeting in the CSB, or at a meeting in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: I think it was said at the CSB, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. You had, however, visited Prijedor. Did you go and visit these camps?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Why was that? Why didn't you go?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Well, that wasn't my duty, my task. And I thought I didn't need to, that it was sufficient for me to write a report. And then if there was some intervention to be made, or conclusions to be made, or order, then, on the basis of that report of mine, that's what would happen. I didn't feel it necessary for me to tour the camps.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you told us that the first report went to the office of the minister. What about the second report? Did that go to the office of the minister?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, others had to go to the minister's office. The cabinet, not the office, the minister's cabinet.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mm-hm. And you told us earlier there was a second meeting with Mico Stanisic. Well, there was a second meeting at which -- just --

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Directly into the hands of the minister. But when you say "office or cabinet," then that's something else.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry. Did you -- are you saying you handed this report directly into the hands of the minister?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was a second meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Let's -- I'm afraid it's my fault because I had -- I hadn't seen that you were carrying on talking.

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: You misunderstood me. Not the minister's office, but to his cabinet. Cabinet.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's roll this back. To whom did you actually hand your first report, the one of the 3rd [sic] of August?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Well, Madam Prosecutor, I can't remember. It was in the minister's cabinet. Now, who received the report, who took possession of it, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I said the 3rd; it's -- sorry, I should have said the 5th. All right. This report dated the 10th of August, to whom did you give that report?

utterances.speaker: SRETO GAJIC
utterances.text: Also to the minister's cabinet.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can we go back to the first page of the report. You say in the third paragraph there: "After introducing the decision made by the Ministry of the Interior at a meeting held on the 6th of August, 1992 ..." So between your report of the 5th of August and this one of the 10th of August, there had apparently, according to you, been a meeting on the 6th. Were you at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm -- I'm terribly sorry, Ms. Korner. Could you please advise us from where do you reading this? Because it doesn't appear in the Serbian original. If we're talking about the 65 ter 10394?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
